text:
Maria: Heads up — we're seeing a rolling p95 spike for customer acme-pro in prod-us-west-2 since ~06:20 UTC. Support ticket #8792. Traces point at a big jump in KV/prefix cache miss rate, up ~3x. Anyone oncall?
Sam: On it. Can you paste the grafana dashboard link? :eyes:
Maria: https://grafana.company/r/abcd123 - p95 jumped from 45ms -> 220ms, p99 to ~800ms. Window 06:15-06:30. Release note: rolled runtime 2.4.1 earlier today. Also noticed more unique prefix keys in logs (session-id in X-Client header?).
SRE-Bot: Alert: eviction_rate high on shard=12, pod=runtime-12b. Sample eviction log: ```evict key=prefix:acct:acme-pro:user:session:7f3a ttl=3s reason=hotset-evict``` repeated 2500x in 5m.
Jon: Is this multi-tenant hotset thrash? If session IDs are leaking into the prefix key, cardinality explodes and we thrash the warmup. Can we repro on stage?
Anya: I can reproduce locally. Quick repro steps I used: ```bash
# generate many unique prefixes by rotating session id
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  curl -s -H "X-Client: session-$i" https://stage-api.internal/acme-pro/complete >/dev/null &
done
# then run a small load to observe cold misses
siege -c50 -t30S https://stage-api.internal/acme-pro/complete
```
Sam: Running that now against a canary stage copy. Seeing p95 climb from 60ms -> 260ms and miss rate shows ~4x increase. Logs show frequent evictions and immediate reinsertions. Looks like TTL is too short and eviction policy not preserving transient hot keys.
Maria: Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase hotset TTL (kv.hot_ttl) from 5s -> 30s for routing rules affecting acme-pro, 2) stagger warmup on shard allocation to avoid simultaneous eviction, 3) add quick prefix normalization to drop session-id from the cache key. Which can we push quickly?
Jon: I can bump kv.hot_ttl for the customer routing policy and restrict the canary to Dedicated pool A. I'll own the config change. Sam can you run a canary test after I flip it? @Sam
Sam: Canary started. Applying config diff: ```diff
- kv.hot_ttl: 5s
+ kv.hot_ttl: 30s
routing:
  acme-pro:
    pool: dedicated-A
```
SRE-Bot: Canary deploy succeeded on runtime-12b-canary. Metrics (2m post-deploy): prefix_miss_rate down 52%, p95 down 40% :thumbsup:
Maria: Good short-term. Longer term we need: prefix canonicalization to strip session-like tokens, sticky-shard affinity for known high-cardinality routes, and a warmed-cache drip policy. I'll file an RFC and tag runtime + infra.
Anya: I'll draft the support update for ACME with repro steps, the temporary kv.hot_ttl workaround, and expected ETA for the RFC. Ticket #8792 will be updated.
Maria: Thanks all. If the problem resurfaces after the TTL bump, we'll open a postmortem. For now, monitor p95/p99 across regions and list of affected customers. Closing the immediate escalation. :white_check_mark:
